source.title: ReMoE: Fully Differentiable Mixture-of-Experts with ReLU Routing
source.authors: Zi-Teng Wang; Jian-Fei Chen; Jun Zhu

record.tranche_reason: The study varies active model size and reports validation loss and downstream accuracy, but does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting procedure.
record.gate_note: The study reports loss curves and scaling sweeps for expert count and granularity as well as active parameters. Only the active-parameter validation-loss sweep bears on V1; downstream accuracy across active sizes bears on V6. Expert-count and granularity comparisons are not tests of parameter/token/compute power laws. Training-loss curves are not held-out pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: This is a routing-method paper (ReLU vs TopK MoE). Its size sweep uses three dense backbones (182M, 469M, 978M), spanning less than one order of magnitude at a fixed 30B tokens. It fits no power law, extrapolates nothing and derives no compute-optimal split. The sweeps exist to show ReMoE's advantage over MoE persists, so the results measure the study's own method against baselines, not whether any scaling-law version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that ReMoE consistently outperforms TopK-routed MoE across active sizes (182M–978M), expert counts (4–128) and granularities (1–64). They also conclude that it scales more steeply with expert count and shows dynamic expert allocation and domain specialization.
record.recipe_differences: This is a comparison of ReLU-routed and TopK-routed MoE language models, not a reproduction of the original dense-language-model scaling-law fit. The active-parameter sweep uses three sizes and fixed 30B-token training.

fits_no_version.finding: At 30B tokens, validation loss falls monotonically from 182M to 978M active parameters for Dense, MoE and ReMoE (about 2.04→1.82, 1.94→1.73 and 1.92→1.72). Average downstream accuracy also rises at each size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over a narrow (<10x) range, loss and average accuracy improve monotonically with active parameters in dense and MoE LMs. This is consistent with, but not a test of, a power law.

record.problems: The active-parameter sweep spans only 182M to 978M and provides no fitted exponents or extrapolation test. The loss sweep's values are presented in a figure rather than stated numerically in the text. Downstream task results are mixed despite increasing average accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: The 21 individual Dense downstream task scores in Table 8 were omitted to remain within the 60-row limit. Tables 9-10 and Figures 6b-6c report expert-count and granularity sweeps, which do not test the listed parameter/token/compute scaling versions; other appendix comparisons are outside those versions.

untested.parts: Power-law form, token and compute scaling, and multi-order-of-magnitude range; only three sizes are run, with no fit.
A predictive relation between scale or loss and downstream accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The record's V1 limits_scope label rested on the study not testing the power law, which belongs under untested, not limits_scope. Its V6 labels rested on a three-point monotone trend without any predictability test. Fig 6a values are readable from the figure text, so the rows' 'figure only' is wrong. Appendix C (469M at 120B tokens, loss 1.716 MoE and 1.689 ReMoE) uses a different batch size and is also a method comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Token-count and compute scaling; fitting or testing a power-law form; several orders of magnitude.
The study does not fit a predictive relationship between pretraining loss and downstream performance.

relation.reason: Section 4.1 uses Krajewski et al.'s compute-optimal dataset prediction; Section 4.3 uses prior fine-grained MoE scaling findings. Its own sweeps evaluate ReMoE's comparative performance without testing a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study uses an existing compute-optimal dataset prediction to choose training duration and reports routing-method comparisons. It does not test power-law form, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or downstream predictability.

source_check.notes: The sampled rows match the source but describe method comparisons rather than tests of the claim versions. Section 4.3 extends MoE baseline training to match ReMoE's computation, so the baseline does not use exactly the same token budget.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Active-parameter sweep from 182M to 978M, with training fixed at 30B tokens
reader_labels.reason: The sweep covers less than one order of magnitude and the study does not fit a power law; plotted values are not numerically stated in the text (r1-r9).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Average zero-shot accuracy across the listed downstream tasks, for Dense, MoE and ReMoE at 182M, 469M and 978M active parameters
reader_labels.reason: The reported average accuracy rises at each successive tested size for all three model types (r10-r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Individual downstream task accuracies for MoE and ReMoE
reader_labels.reason: Several task scores decline or stop increasing at the largest size, so the average trend does not hold uniformly across tasks (r26, r36, r39, r48, r60).
